I had the same question. The inlined version appears to call the hooks
unconditionally and in a consistent order, so it's not immediately obvious
which Rule of React would be violated. If the compiler is intentionally
bailing out here, it would be helpful to understand the specific analysis
limitation or safety concern that causes it to treat the two forms
differently.

On Wed, Jul 1, 2026, 5:40 AM jaxonfenwick297-pixel ***@***.***>
wrote:

> *jaxonfenwick297-pixel* left a comment (react/react#36847)
> <https://github.com/react/react/issues/36847#issuecomment-4853445169>
> Could you clarify which specific Rules of React are being violated in the
> inlined example?
>
> While the LLM explanation provides some general context, it would be
> helpful to understand exactly why the compiler treats the inlined version
> differently than the version with separate variables, as both appear to
> follow standard hook patterns.
>

> > The React compiler relies on assumptions about dependencies and pure
> > functions to provide memoization; when the assumptions are not met, the
> > compiler will bail out. React is compiled to "just JS" at the end of the
> > day, and JS allows you to do a lot of dynamic stuff that can be
> sub-optimal.
